claude.sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

links.outcome: Performance drop from internal to external knee X-ray dataset under domain shift
links.effect: External AUC 0.72–0.89 but accuracy only 31–44%, indicating calibration drift and domain shift between internal and external datasets.
links.quote: Although most models achieved relatively high AUC values (0.72–0.89), the corresponding external test accuracy remained substantially lower (31–44%), suggesting the presence of calibration drift and domain shift between the internal and external datasets.

links.outcome: Osteopenia recall and balanced accuracy after class-prior boosting and recalibration on external data
links.effect: Class-prior boosting raised balanced accuracy from 38.0% to 48.0%, macro F1 from 0.259 to 0.416, and Osteopenia recall from 2% to 78%; Normal recall fell from 22% to 6%. Recalibration alone was insufficient.
links.quote: Most importantly, Osteopenia recall improved dramatically from 2% to 78%, transforming the model from effectively blind to the intermediate disease stage into a clinically meaningful early-detection screening system.

links.outcome: Calibration drift under external domain shift
links.effect: Osteopenia predicted probabilities collapsed below 0.30 externally, with baseline Osteopenia recall of 2%; Osteoporosis class overconfident.
links.quote: From Table 10 , reliability analysis revealed that the Osteopenia class experienced near-complete probability collapse, with predicted probabilities consistently remaining below 0.30 during external testing.

links.outcome: Overestimated performance from internal versus external validation
links.effect: Internal test accuracy about 67–75% versus external accuracy 31–44%; external set was isolated and used once, revealing a performance gap.
links.quote: This limitation is reflected in the observed performance gap between internal and external validation, highlighting the challenges of generalization across different imaging domains.

links.outcome: Discrimination (AUC) masking poor calibration and threshold-based performance
links.effect: High external AUC (0.87–0.89) masked poor threshold-based accuracy (~42–43%); subgroup/class-specific Osteopenia sensitivity was near zero.
links.quote: Importantly, high discrimination performance should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical readiness.

unlisted_practices: Class-prior boosting with cross-validated threshold optimization for external domain shift

links.effect: AUC 0.72–0.89 but external accuracy 31–44%, revealing calibration drift and domain shift.
links.quote: Although most models achieved relatively high AUC values (0.72–0.89), the corresponding external test accuracy remained substantially lower (31–44%), suggesting the presence of calibration drift and domain shift between the internal and external datasets.

links.effect: External dataset lacked acquisition protocols, equipment, DXA procedures, quality control, and label generation details.
links.quote: As the dataset was collected and curated by an independent source, detailed information regarding image acquisition protocols, imaging equipment, DXA procedures, image quality control, and label generation was not fully available.

links.effect: AUC 0.87–0.89 while external classification accuracy was approximately 42–43%.
links.quote: While several models achieved relatively high AUC values (0.87–0.89), external classification accuracy remained limited (approximately 42–43%).

links.effect: DenseNet-121+Neural Network had highest test accuracy 75.38, F1-score 72.45, AUC 0.9010.
links.quote: Similarly, DenseNet-121 with Neural Network delivers the best overall performance, achieving the highest test accuracy (75.38) and F1-score (72.45), along with the highest AUC (0.9010), demonstrating superior generalization and feature learning capability.

links.effect: Domain shift led to external accuracy 31–44% despite AUC 0.72–0.89.
links.quote: Although most models achieved relatively high AUC values (0.72–0.89), the corresponding external test accuracy remained substantially lower (31–44%), suggesting the presence of calibration drift and domain shift between the internal and external datasets.

links.effect: Overall and balanced accuracy increased 38.0% to 48.0%; macro F1 0.259 to 0.416.
links.quote: From Table 11 , the CV-unbiased evaluation demonstrated that class-prior adjustment increased overall accuracy and balanced accuracy from 38.0% to 48.0%, while macro F1-score improved from 0.259 to 0.416.

links.effect: Normal recall improved 14% to 22%, but Osteopenia recall remained 2%.
links.quote: Although recalibration improved Normal recall from 14% to 22%, Osteopenia recall remained unchanged at only 2%, indicating that probability recalibration alone was insufficient to recover the suppressed Osteopenia decision region under external domain shift (see Table 9 ).

links.effect: External accuracy approximately 42–43% despite AUC 0.87–0.89.
links.quote: Although AUC values remained relatively high under external testing, the substantially reduced classification accuracy indicates that many individual predictions would still be incorrect in practice.

unlisted_practices: Training-set data augmentation and oversampling/class balancing to mitigate class imbalance

links.outcome: external test accuracy drop under domain shift
links.effect: External test accuracy dropped substantially to 31–44% despite relatively high AUC values (0.72–0.89), demonstrating severe performance degradation on external validation data.
links.quote: Although most models achieved relatively high AUC values (0.72–0.89), the corresponding external test accuracy remained substantially lower (31–44%), suggesting the presence of calibration drift and domain shift between the internal and external datasets.

links.effect: Models showed a substantial discrepancy between AUC and threshold-based metrics, with severe probability collapse in osteopenia concealed by high AUC values.
links.quote: External validation revealed a substantial discrepancy between AUC and threshold-based metrics, indicating the presence of calibration drift and class-prior mismatch across imaging domains.

unlisted_practices: Post-hoc isotonic recalibration and class-prior boosting with threshold optimization to address calibration drift and class-prior mismatch under domain shift
